chronology: [Recap] Aghnar, the current Metabaron, kills Janus-Jana's guards and renounces imperial service, becoming a mercenary for hire across many clients over years.
[Recap] Aghnar, aging on his natal planet Anasirma, accepts a Pthagurean genocide contract to exterminate all life in the Empire in exchange for payment.

[Recap] The Empire, unable to defeat Aghnar, accepts a Techno-Techno proposal: Steelhead, Aghnar's son, is revealed as humanity's champion. He reshapes the Imperial dome into a golden flower as a demonstration of power. A duel is arranged with fleets massing around each side's metacraft.

[Frame story] Robots Tonto and Lothar at the Metabunker, in the ruins of Terra 2014's city-shaft, realize the Metabaron has not returned on schedule and activate a bio-electrogram to check his status. Tonto recounts the duel.
[Story-within-story] A meca-womb is charged with energotromes and the Metabaron's bio-electrogram is activated; he destroys a large number of cerbomaks per second during a test.
[Story-within-story] Lothar manifests as a devastating holographic form, destroys all cerebomaks in under a minute, and fouls an opposing ship's firing tubes with tentacle-like appendages.

[Story-within-story] Aghnar, with Oda-Honorada aboard, readies his metacraft for the formal duel. Oda-Honorada frames the confrontation as the Metabaron rite in which a son proves stronger than his father.

[Story-within-story] The Supreme Pthagurean Triumvirate and the imperial couple jointly authorize the match from a neutral diplomatic vessel. After massive weapons fire, both combatants act in apparent mutual accord and generate a black hole that swallows them.

[Story-within-story] The combatants' weapons rupture space, opening a breach into inter-space. They traverse a region of infinite geometric straight lines, a chaotic amber zone, and the dimension of origins before resuming their destructive exchange.

[Story-within-story] Both metacraft drift recklessly to the Omphall, the mystical cosmic center. The Omphall engulfs and immediately expels both craft. They hang motionless facing each other while millions of human and Ptaguan spectators wait in tense silence.

[Story-within-story] A mother figure uses a mega-hypnotic head and transmits psychic power via probe against an armored opponent. Steelhead resists, threatening his own molecular unity. The mother depletes all remaining psychotrons in a final escalation.

[Story-within-story] A warship destroys an opposing vessel. Non-human spectators celebrate humanity's end prematurely. An official insists the duel is unfinished until Aghnar kills his son. In space amid wreckage, the son yields honorably to Aghnar, offering his life.

[Story-within-story] A cybernetic antagonist seizes Oda, vessel of Honorata's spirit, and uses her as leverage against Aghnar, threatening to dismember her piece by piece. Aghnar denounces the tactic; the antagonist rejects all warrior codes.
[Story-within-story] The cybernetic antagonist systematically severs all ten of Oda's fingers, ranting that his humanity was taken from him.

[Story-within-story] Aghnar pleads for Oda's release. A cybernetic warrior broadcasts via hyper-megaphone to millions of ships, declaring himself the supreme Metabaron of the Castaka line, condemning his father Othon as dishonorable, and requesting an honorable death. A mercenary bystander dismisses honor.

[Story-within-story] The woman condemns the son's victory as treachery, declaring he has lost her and the entire Metabarons clan. She then reverses and says she will accompany him even into death. Both drift into open space.

[Story-within-story] Two armored figures embrace and simultaneously detonate internal mini-bombs, producing a galaxy-scale explosion. A narrator celebrates the sacrifice; another reorients the story toward Aghnar's beginning.
[Aftermath] Humanity is saved but the Pthagurean race is ended. A Pthagurean spokesperson orders fleet-wide immediate mass suicide. The fleet obeys, self-destructing in a vast ring of fire.

[Aftermath] The three Pthagurean Triumvirate members are expelled into space. Steelhead, victorious but publicly unrecognized and bitter, departs with reward treasure on course for the Metabunker. Soldiers celebrate their survival.

[New arc] A victory ball is held aboard the diplomatic vessel for the imperial couple. Translucent vampires penetrate the netranekkon armor, invade the hall, and consume guests' brains. Armed defenders cannot stop them.

[New arc] At the Metabunker over the deserts of Sirtha, Steelhead tries on helmets to mask his weapon-head anatomy while Tonto advises him. An urgent galactic transmission from the new Golden Palace requests an audience. Steelhead responds immediately.

[New arc] A holographic neocerth empress tells Steelhead the duel with Aghnar opened a reality breach and devourers from inter-space threaten the universe. Steelhead negotiates for the title Supreme Metabaron and a high nobility medallion requiring unanimous planetary ambassador consent. The empress identifies Don Nicanor Rosamel de Rokha of the Under-Developed Petroglotosocialik Federation as the sole obstacle. Steelhead concludes he must eliminate this man.
[New arc] Steelhead seals the interspace breach; vampires, cut off from their energy source, disintegrate. His cybernetic nature made him immune to their mind-targeting attack.

[New arc] Steelhead infiltrates the Troglosocialik defense system via poly-cloaked psy-glider over the capital planet Philodendra. Robotic observers accuse him of having murdered Nacnor Rosaamel de Rokha, the last planar Tay priest.
[New arc] Steelhead approaches the Halerce Tree under three suns; its golden canopy is revealed to be millions of legendary Djykka-birds.
[New arc] Steelhead fires a Cerebrak IK-8 at the supreme Troglosocialik president during morning meditation among the Djykka-birds.
[Closing] A massive explosion follows. All planetary ambassadors unanimously award high nobility to Othon von Salza for saving humanity twice. Next episode announced: Steelhead's Quest.
locations: The Metabunker — suspended in the ruins of the city-shaft on Terra 2014; the frame-story setting where Tonto and Lothar narrate events
Biomechanical activation chamber containing a meca-womb and glowing basin where the Metabaron is tested
The Imperial Palace — site of Aghnar's defection from imperial service (recap)
Anasirma — Aghnar's natal planet, reduced to its last remains
Outer space — primary arena for the formal duel, observed from a neutral diplomatic vessel
Inter-space — the essential fabric of the universe, accessed by breaching normal space
The region of infinite geometric straight lines within inter-space
The dimension of origins — an inner realm of living lights accessible through inter-space
The Omphall — the mystical cosmic center of beginning and end
The neutral diplomatic vessel serving as the observation point for the match
The diplomatic vessel's grand ceremonial ballroom — site of the imperial victory ball and the vampire attack
The Metabunker drifting over the deserts of Sirtha
The new Golden Palace — source of the holographic imperial transmission
Philodendra — capital planet of the Troglosocialik federation, with villages harmonized with non-artificial forests
The Halerce Tree — on a world with three suns, described as the oldest tree in the galaxy
A grand ceremonial council chamber where planetary ambassadors convene to award Othon von Salza high nobility
lore_laws: The Metabaron lineage follows a succession rite: a son is not fully recognized until he defeats his father in combat.
A meca-womb charged with energotromes can activate or manifest a Metabaron through a bio-electrogram process.
Cerbomaks/cerebomaks are intelligent creatures deployed in large numbers as test subjects or weapons; the Metabaron can destroy several per second.
Metacraft are piloted through intimate bodily or neural linkage, not only conventional controls.

Inter-space is the essential fabric of the universe; sufficiently powerful attacks can breach into it. Its region of infinite geometric straight lines requires entrants to become filament-like to traverse.
The Omphall is a mystical cosmic center of origin and annihilation; metacraft can physically approach it but doing so is extremely dangerous.
Mini-bombs can be implanted inside a body; two individuals detonating simultaneously produce a catastrophic explosion.
Steelhead's head is composed of or includes deadly weapons; helmets are worn to mask this.

Vampiric beings from inter-space pass through netranekkon armor, consume victims' brains, and rely on a spatial breach as an energy source; sealing the breach destroys them. They cannot affect a largely cybernetic host.
The Pthagureans can execute organized fleet-wide mass suicide on command from their leadership.
A medallion of high nobility requires unanimous consent from all planetary ambassadors to be awarded.
A hyper-megaphone can broadcast to millions of spaceships simultaneously.
A weapon called the Cerebrak IK-8 exists and is used for assassination.
A poly-cloaked psy-glider can penetrate outdated planetary defense systems undetected.
The Halerce Tree on a three-sun world is described as the oldest tree in the galaxy; its apparent golden canopy consists of millions of legendary Djykka-birds singing together.
Psychotrons are a finite reserve weapon system; psychic power can be transmitted and amplified through a probe from one being to another.
A mega-hypnotic head device can be used offensively to paralyze an opponent and threaten molecular unity.
The dimension of origins, accessible through inter-space, contains only living lights and is characterized as purely calm until violated by outside conflict.
major_events: The Supreme Pthagurean Triumvirate and the imperial couple jointly authorize the formal duel between Aghnar and Steelhead, observed by millions of human and Ptaguan spectators from a neutral diplomatic vessel.

The duel ruptures normal space, carrying both combatants through inter-space, the dimension of infinite straight lines, and the dimension of origins, before both are swallowed and expelled by the Omphall.
Steelhead, humanity's champion, is defeated by Aghnar and yields honorably in open space, offering his life to his father.
A cybernetic antagonist tortures Oda (vessel of Honorata's spirit) by severing her fingers, weaponizing family bonds to break Aghnar.
Two armored figures embrace and simultaneously detonate internal mini-bombs, producing a galaxy-scale explosion that closes their arc.
The Pthagurean fleet carries out coordinated mass suicide on command, ending the galactic threat and saving humanity. The three Triumvirate members are expelled into space.
Steelhead seals the interspace breach opened by the duel, defeating translucent vampire invaders who are immune to conventional weapons but unable to affect his cybernetic body.
Steelhead assassinates Don Nicanor Rosamel de Rokha and the supreme Troglosocialik president to remove political obstacles to his elevation.
All planetary ambassadors unanimously award high nobility to Othon von Salza for saving humanity twice from total annihilation.
open_uncertainties: The precise relationship between Steelhead and Othon von Salza is not resolved: it is unclear whether they are the same character or different generations, and how the warrior on p16 who names his father as Othon fits the lineage.
The identities of the two armored figures who jointly detonate mini-bombs are not explicitly confirmed by the page summaries.

The exact outcome of the duel is disputed within the story itself: one speaker insists Aghnar won; another rejects that conclusion and argues the Phagureans would have annihilated humanity if it were true.
The identity and name of the cybernetic antagonist who tortures Oda remain unknown from the pages.
Whether the holographic attacking form of Lothar in the duel sequence is the same character as the robot Lothar at the Metabunker is not explicitly stated.

Several proper names have uncertain spellings due to image resolution: Pthagureans/Phagureans/Ptaguans, Oda-Honorada/Honoratza/Honorata, Anasirma, Troglosocialik, Petroglotosocialik, Nacnor/Nicanor Rosaamel/Rosamel de Rokha.
The nature of the black triangular craft near the sealed interspace breach is not identified.
It is not confirmed from the pages whether the supreme Troglosocialik president and Don Nicanor Rosamel de Rokha are the same person or separate targets.
Several printed page numbers visible in the art differ from the supplied page labels, suggesting a possible discrepancy in the numbering scheme.
recurring_motifs: Father-son combat as Metabaron rite: a son must prove himself mightier than his father to be recognized within the lineage
Honor versus treachery: repeated confrontation between characters upholding warrior codes and those treating any tactic as valid if it achieves victory
Neural and bodily integration with metacraft: pilots connect through intimate physical linkage, not conventional controls
Escalating cosmic geography: the duel traverses normal space, inter-space, geometric dimensions, and the dimension of origins, each realm more primordial than the last
The Omphall as axis of creation and annihilation: a cosmic center that swallows and expels even the most powerful combatants
Robotic narrators as frame device: Tonto and Lothar at the Metabunker mediate the reader's access to past events through storytelling and argument
Sacrifice and self-destruction as honorable ending: characters choose mutual self-annihilation over survival under dishonor
Transactional heroism: Steelhead refuses altruism and demands personal advancement before acting to save the universe
Lineage and clan identity as legitimation and burden: the Castaka/Metabaron line is invoked to condemn, justify, and measure every act
title: Clash of the Meta-Warriors
